assignedReviews.card_evidence: inside their gizzard, the sand grinds the food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes mechanical grinding in a worm's gizzard, which is a digestive process, but it does not use a labeled diagram to trace food through the digestive tract, nor does it cover the human digestive tract or the range of processes (secretion, digestion, absorption, elimination) required by the competency. The format requirement (labeled diagram) is not met, so this is at most related_only.

copy.en:
How do worms chew without teeth?

Worms have no teeth! They swallow soft food along with tiny grains of sand — inside their gizzard, the sand grinds the food, just like teeth working inside the belly.
copy.tl:
Paano ngumunguya ang bulate kung walang ngipin?

Walang ngipin ang bulate, kaya nilalamon nito ang malambot na pagkain at maliliit na butil ng buhangin. Sa loob ng gizzard nito, ginigiling ng buhangin ang pagkain — parang ngipin na nasa loob ng tiyan.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglamoy sa ulod kung walay ngipon?

Walay ngipon ang ulod, mao nga molamoy kini og humok nga pagkaon ug gagmay nga lugas sa balas. Sulod sa ilang gizzard, galingon sa balas ang pagkaon — sama sa ngipon nga naa sa sulod sa tiyan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Table salt is safe to eat, even though it's made from dangerous sodium and chlorine.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of ions as either the loss or gain of electrons to produce ionic bonds, using examples, such as the formation of sodium chloride
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that a compound (table salt) has different properties from its constituent elements (sodium, chlorine). It does not explain the formation of ions via loss/gain of electrons or the production of ionic bonds, which is the core of G9-M-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Table salt is safe to eat, even though it's made from dangerous sodium and chlorine.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical names of some common ionic compounds, including sodium chloride (NaCl), magnesium oxide (MgO), potassium chloride (KCl) and magnesium chloride (MgCl2)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sodium and chlorine forming table salt but does not write the chemical formula (NaCl) or chemical name, nor does it address any other ionic compound. It does not support the skill of writing formulas/names.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When atoms bond, the new compound has totally different properties!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons

It does not describe pure substances as having fixed chemical composition or that all atoms of an element have a unique number of protons, the specific requirements of G8-M-4.

copy.en: When atoms bond, the new compound has totally different properties! Table salt is safe to eat, even though it's made from dangerous sodium and chlorine.
copy.tl: Kapag nagbi-bond ang mga atomo, ang compound na nabubuo ay may ibang katangian! Ligtas kainin ang asin, kahit galing ito sa mapanganib na sodium at chlorine.
copy.bis: Kon magbugkos ang mga atomo, ang compound nga maporma adunay lahi nga kinaiya! Luwas kaonon ang asin, bisan gama kini sa delikado nga sodium ug chlorine.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air particles are bunched close together with high pressure. In a rarefaction, particles are spread apart with low pressure!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify differences and similarities between longitudinal waves and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes compressions and rarefactions, which are features of longitudinal waves, but it does not compare longitudinal and transverse waves or identify any similarities/differences between them. It provides no information about transverse waves.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air particles are bunched close together with high pressure. In a rarefaction, particles are spread apart with low pressure!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate using simple models how longitudinal waves and transverse waves carry energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes particle behavior in compressions and rarefactions but does not demonstrate using a model how longitudinal or transverse waves carry energy. No model or energy transfer is addressed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air particles are bunched close together with high pressure. In a rarefaction, particles are spread apart with low pressure!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some examples of longitudinal waves, and transverse waves
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a property of sound waves (compressions/rarefactions) but does not identify examples of longitudinal or transverse waves. It does not name sound as a longitudinal wave or give any other examples.

copy.en:
What happens to air particles in a compression and rarefaction?

Air particles are bunched close together with high pressure. In a rarefaction, particles are spread apart with low pressure!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa mga particle ng hangin sa compression at rarefaction?

Ang mga particle ng hangin ay siksik at mataas ang presyon. Sa rarefaction, ang mga particle ay malayo sa isa't isa at mababa ang presyon!
copy.bis:
Unsay nahitabo sa mga particle sa hangin sa compression ug rarefaction?

Ang mga particle sa hangin nasiksik ug taas ang presyon. Sa rarefaction, ang mga particle nagbulag ug ubos ang presyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ancient Romans were the first to use it to build amazing structures!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the ancient Romans first used concrete widely. It does not use information from the home or local community, does not identify concrete as a science invention in that context, and does not explain its impact on everyday life. The content is historically related to a material but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Who were the very first people to use concrete widely?

The ancient Romans were the first to use it to build amazing structures!
copy.tl:
Sino ang mga unang tao na malawakang gumamit ng konkreto?

Ang mga sinaunang Romano ang unang gumamit nito!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang mga unang tawo nga naggamit og konkreto sa kaylap?

Ang karaang mga Romano ang unang naggamit niini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The dew point is the temperature where water vapour in the air condenses into water drops!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes condensation (water vapour to liquid) but does not use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency. It only mentions condensation in the context of dew point, not the full set of state changes (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) with the required representations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When the air gets colder than the dew point, dew forms.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on temperature causing a change of state (condensation), but the competency focuses on solid-liquid-gas changes (e.g., melting, evaporation) and does not specifically require condensation. The card does not describe the general temperature-driven state changes across solids, liquids, and gases.

copy.en:
What is the dew point, and how does dew form?

The dew point is the temperature where water vapour in the air condenses into water drops! When the air gets colder than the dew point, dew forms.
copy.tl:
Ano ang dew point, at paano nabubuo ang hamog?

Ang dew point ay ang temperatura kung saan nagiging patak ng tubig ang water vapour sa hangin! Kapag mas malamig ang hangin kaysa dew point, lumalabas ang hamog.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang dew point, ug unsaon paghimo sa hamog?

Ang dew point mao ang temperatura diin ang water vapour sa hangin nahimong patak sa tubig! Kung mas bugnaw ang hangin kaysa dew point, mogawas ang hamog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the droplets from condensation in clouds grow large and heavy enough to drop
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions condensation but does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) for solids, liquids, and gases, nor does it use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency. It only uses condensation as a step in rain formation, providing no direct instructional support for the state-change processes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rain falls when the droplets from condensation in clouds grow large and heavy enough to drop
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains one step of the water cycle (condensation leading to precipitation) but does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment. It gives no information about how the water cycle functions as a whole or its environmental significance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rain falls when the droplets from condensation in clouds grow large and heavy enough to drop
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct a model to communicate some of the key processes in the water cycle
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not construct a model or communicate key processes of the water cycle. It only states a fact about rain formation; no model, drawing, or representation is involved.

copy.en:
How do clouds make rain fall down to us?

Rain falls when the droplets from condensation in clouds grow large and heavy enough to drop!
copy.tl:
Kailan bumababa ang ulan mula sa mga ulap?

Umuulan kapag ang mga patak mula sa paghalumigmig sa ulap ay lumaki at bumigat hanggang mahulog!
copy.bis:
Kanus-a mahulog ang ulan gikan sa panganod?

Moulan kung ang mga tulo gikan sa pamuo sa panganod modako ug mobug-at hangtod nga mahulog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heat travels in three ways: conduction through touching particles, convection by moving heated fluids, and radiation through electromagnetic waves that need no matter!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines the three modes of heat transfer but gives no examples and no advantageous or disadvantageous applications, so it only provides background for identifying such examples.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: conduction through touching particles, convection by moving heated fluids
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions conduction and convection and hints at particle/fluid movement, but it does not explain the processes in terms of the particle model (e.g., particle vibration, collisions, density changes), so it is background rather than direct instruction.

copy.en: Heat travels in three ways: conduction through touching particles, convection by moving heated fluids, and radiation through electromagnetic waves that need no matter!
copy.tl: Ang init ay naglalakbay sa tatlong paraan: conduction sa touching particles, convection sa paggalaw ng heated fluids, at radiation sa electromagnetic waves na hindi nangangailangan ng matter!
copy.bis: Ang init mobalhin sa tulo ka paagi: conduction sa touching particles, convection sa paglihok sa heated fluids, ug radiation sa electromagnetic waves nga dili kinahanglan og matter!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In conduction, heat passes through materials that touch, moving fast through metal but slow through air or plastic!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card only describes the basic behavior of conduction (fast in metal, slow in air/plastic). It does not identify any advantageous or disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, or radiation, which is the specific skill of G7-F-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In conduction, heat passes through materials that touch, moving fast through metal but slow through air or plastic!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions conduction and gives a qualitative comparison of speed in different materials, but it does not explain the process using the particle model (e.g., particle vibration, energy transfer between particles). It lacks the explanatory mechanism required by G7-F-10.

copy.en: In conduction, heat passes through materials that touch, moving fast through metal but slow through air or plastic!
copy.tl: Sa conduction, dumadaan ang heat sa mga magkadikit na materyales, mabilis sa metal pero mabagal sa air o plastic!
copy.bis: Sa conduction, ang heat moagi sa mga materyales nga naghikap, paspas sa metal apan hinay sa air o plastic!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Conductive hearing loss happens when sound is blocked in the outer or middle ear and is often treatable.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how light and sound can be harmful to people and make suggestions on how to protect oneself from them
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes types of hearing loss but does not explain how sound can be harmful or suggest protective measures. It only mentions that one type is treatable and the other permanent, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sensorineural loss comes from cochlea or nerve damage and is usually permanent.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses hearing loss and ear anatomy, but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It is about hearing impairment, not sound production or transmission.

copy.en: Conductive hearing loss happens when sound is blocked in the outer or middle ear and is often treatable. Sensorineural loss comes from cochlea or nerve damage and is usually permanent.
copy.tl: Nangyayari ang conductive hearing loss kapag nahahadlangan ang tunog sa outer o middle ear at madalas nagagamot. Ang sensorineural hearing loss ay galing sa pinsala ng cochlea o nerve at kadalasang permanente.
copy.bis: Mahitabo ang conductive hearing loss kung mahadlangan ang tunog sa outer o middle ear ug kasagaran ginaayo. Ang sensorineural hearing loss gikan sa samad sa cochlea o nerve ug kasagaran permanente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: important for safety!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe and explain the need for safety precautions in handling household electrical devices
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wire color codes and says they are important for safety, but it does not describe or explain the need for safety precautions in handling household electrical devices. It is only tangentially related to electrical safety.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: important for safety!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons, nor does it teach safe measures in handling electricity beyond noting that wire colors are important for safety. It does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Philippine wires are color-coded
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wires but does not involve assembling or drawing a simple circuit, nor does it use the required format of an assembled/drawn circuit. Wire color coding is background knowledge at most, not direct support for circuit construction.

copy.en: Philippine wires are color-coded: live is brown or red, neutral is blue or black, ground is green or yellow-and-green — important for safety!
copy.tl: May color code ang mga kawad sa Pilipinas: live ay brown o red, neutral ay blue o black, ground ay green o yellow-and-green — mahalaga para sa kaligtasan!
copy.bis: Adunay color code ang mga wire sa Pilipinas: live kay brown o red, neutral kay blue o black, ground kay green o yellow-and-green — importante para sa kaligtasan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The law of conservation of energy says energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity, such as when objects fall
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the general law of conservation of energy but does not describe it in everyday situations involving gravity, such as objects falling. It provides useful background but does not directly teach the competency's specific application.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The law of conservation of energy says energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy transformation but does not identify energy as something that can cause change, nor does it mention light, sound, or heat energy. It shares the broad topic of energy but gives no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: The law of conservation of energy says energy cannot be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another!
copy.tl: Ayon sa law of conservation of energy, hindi maaaring likhain o sirain ang enerhiya; nagbabago lamang ito ng anyo!
copy.bis: Sumala sa law of conservation of energy, ang enerhiya dili mahimo o maguba; mausab lang kini og porma!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Only half are up each night, changing by season.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that constellations change by season, which is a pattern of visible stars over a year, but it does not involve making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model or explaining the mechanism behind the seasonal changes. The competency requires a model-based demonstration and explanation, which the card does not provide.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Only half are up each night, changing by season.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that only half of the constellations are visible each night and that they change by season, but it does not guide students to explore and record how and when the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars move across the sky. It is a general fact about constellation visibility, not an activity for observing and recording celestial motion.

copy.en:
Can you see every constellation in just one night?

Nope! Only half are up each night, changing by season. You need to watch the sky across different months to see most of them!
copy.tl:
Makikita mo ba lahat ng constellation sa isang gabi?

Hindi! Kalahati lang ang nasa langit bawat gabi, at nag-iiba sa bawat season. Kailangan mong magbantay sa iba't ibang buwan para makita ang karamihan!
copy.bis:
Makita ba nimo ang tanang constellation sa usa ka gabii?

Dili! Katunga lang ang naa sa langit matag gabii, ug nagailis kada season. Kinahanglan nimo motan-aw sa lain-laing bulan aron makita ang kadaghanan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: swapping whole constellations month to month? That's Earth orbiting the Sun all year!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the yearly change in visible constellations due to Earth's orbit, which is one of the observable effects listed in the competency. However, the competency requires making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain these effects, and the card does not involve or reference any model. It also omits seasons and eclipses. Thus it only touches the topic without meeting the required activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Each night, stars slide east to west because Earth spins.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate the rotation of the Earth on its axis using a globe to explain day and night
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that nightly star motion is due to Earth's rotation, which is related to the rotation concept in the competency. However, the competency specifically requires demonstrating rotation using a globe to explain day and night. The card does not use a globe, does not mention day and night, and only uses star motion as an example. It does not directly support the required demonstration or explanation.

copy.en: Two moves! Each night, stars slide east to west because Earth spins. But swapping whole constellations month to month? That's Earth orbiting the Sun all year!
copy.tl: Dalawang galaw! Tuwing gabi, dumadaan ang mga bituin mula silangan hanggang kanluran dahil umiikot ang Earth. Pero ang pagpapalit ng buong konstelasyon buwan-buwan? Iyon ay dahil sa pag-ikot ng Earth sa Araw sa loob ng isang taon!
copy.bis: Duha ka lihok! Matag gabii, moagi ang mga bituon gikan sa sidlakan paingon sa kasadpan tungod kay molibot ang Earth. Apan ang pag-ilis sa tibuok konstelasyon matag bulan? Tungod kini sa paglibot sa Earth sa Adlaw sulod sa usa ka tuig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Only WHEN and WHERE we see it in the sky changes through the year.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that constellation shapes stay the same and only visibility changes, which touches on the 'changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year' part of the competency. However, it does not involve making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model, nor does it explain the cause (Earth's motion) or address seasons or eclipses. It provides only a related fact without the required model or explanation.

copy.en:
Do constellations change shape over the year?

Nope! The star pattern stays exactly the same. Only WHEN and WHERE we see it in the sky changes through the year. Orion today looks just like Orion did in ancient times!
copy.tl:
Nagbabago ba ang hugis ng mga konstelasyon sa buong taon?

Hindi! Pareho pa rin ang ayos ng mga bituin. Ang KAILAN at SAAN natin ito nakikita sa langit lang ang nagbabago. Ang Orion ngayon ay pareho ng Orion noong sinaunang panahon!
copy.bis:
Nausab ba ang porma sa mga konstelasyon sulod sa tuig?

Dili! Parehas gihapon ang pattern sa mga bituon. Ang KANUS-A ug ASA nato kini makita sa langit lang ang mausab. Ang Orion karon parehas ra sa Orion sa karaang panahon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Phone apps can show you! The computer tracks Earth's orbit to predict which constellations face us.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars/constellations but does not support the guided activity of observing and describing natural objects in the sky. It focuses on using an app to predict constellations, not on observation or description.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The computer tracks Earth's orbit to predict which constellations face us.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Earth's orbit and constellations, which are part of the competency's content, but it does not involve making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model or demonstrating/explaining predictable patterns such as seasons, star patterns over a year, or eclipses. It only states that apps use Earth's orbit to predict constellations.

copy.en:
Want to know tonight's stars?

Phone apps can show you! The computer tracks Earth's orbit to predict which constellations face us. It's a cool way to learn the sky!
copy.tl:
Gusto mo malaman ang mga bituin ngayong gabi?

May phone apps na pwedeng magpakita! Tinitrack ng computer ang orbit ng Earth para hulaan kung anong constellations ang makikita. Napakagandang paraan para matuto!
copy.bis:
Gusto ka ba mahibal-an ang mga bituon karong gabii?

Adunay phone apps nga makapakita! Gi-track sa computer ang orbit sa Earth aron matagna kung unsang constellations ang makita. Maayong paagi kini sa pagkat-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: some constellations never set and can be seen all year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that some constellations never set and are visible all year near the poles, but it does not describe how or when the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars move across the sky, nor does it involve guided activities to explore and record such motion. The content is about visibility, not movement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: some constellations never set and can be seen all year
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires making a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain observable effects of predictable patterns, including changes in visible star patterns over a year. The card only mentions that some constellations never set near the poles and are not visible from the Philippines; it does not explain the cause, use a model, or address the Sun-Earth-Moon system. It is a related fact about star visibility, not direct support for the competency.

copy.en:
Are there constellations we can see all year round?

Near the Earth's poles, some constellations never set and can be seen all year, but not from the Philippines!
copy.tl:
May mga konstelasyon ba na nakikita buong taon?

Malapit sa mga pole ng Earth, may mga konstelasyon na hindi lumulubog at nakikita buong taon, pero hindi sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis:
Aduna ba mga konstelasyon nga makita tibuok tuig?

Duol sa mga pole sa kalibutan, adunay mga konstelasyon nga dili musalop ug makita tibuok tuig, apan dili sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from local indigenous community members or from reliable secondary sources to investigate ways that indigenous people of the Philippines represented and communicated understandings of the predictability of solar and lunar eclipses, and patterns/interpretations in the night sky and their use for tracking time
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that different cultures see different star patterns. assignedReviews.card_evidence: Different cultures around the world have seen different shapes and patterns in the same stars in the sky!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars and patterns in the sky, but the competency requires guided activities to observe and describe natural objects (Sun, Moon, planets, stars). The card does not support observation or description of these objects; it only notes cultural differences in star patterns. No direct instructional support.

copy.en:
Do different cultures see the same shapes in the stars?

Different cultures around the world have seen different shapes and patterns in the same stars in the sky!
copy.tl:
Nakikita ba ng iba't ibang kultura ang magkakaibang hugis sa mga bituin?

Iba't ibang kultura sa mundo ang nakakita ng magkakaibang hugis at pattern sa parehong mga bituin sa langit!
copy.bis:
Nakakita ba ang nagkalainlaing kultura og lahi-lahing porma sa mga bituon?

Ang nagkalainlaing kultura sa kalibutan nakakita og lahi-lahing porma ug pattern sa samang mga bituon sa langit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many Filipino legends are tied to stars too, like the Balatik!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from local indigenous community members or from reliable secondary sources to investigate ways that indigenous people of the Philippines represented and communicated understandings of the predictability of solar and lunar eclipses, and patterns/interpretations in the night sky and their use for tracking time
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions Filipino star legends (Balatik) and cultural differences in star patterns, which touches on night-sky interpretations. However, it does not address gathering information from indigenous community members or secondary sources, nor does it cover eclipse predictability or time tracking. It only states that different cultures see different pictures, without teaching the investigative or communicative aspects of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Do different cultures see the same pictures in the stars?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses stars and cultural interpretations, but it does not guide students to observe and describe natural objects in the sky (Sun, Moon, planets, stars) as objects. It focuses on cultural stories rather than careful observation and description of celestial objects, so it does not directly support the guided activity of observing and describing.

copy.en:
Do different cultures see the same pictures in the stars?

Nope! What one culture calls a bear, another might see as a ladle. Many Filipino legends are tied to stars too, like the Balatik!
copy.tl:
Nakikita ba ng iba't ibang kultura ang parehong larawan sa mga bituin?

Hindi! Ang tinatawag na oso ng iba, ay maaaring sandok o hayop para sa iba. Maraming Pilipinong alamat ang nakaugnay sa mga bituin tulad ng Balatik!
copy.bis:

Nope! They are at very different distances in space. They only happen to form a shape when seen from Earth!

Hindi! Nasa magkakaibang layo sila sa kalawakan. Nagkataon lang na bumubuo sila ng hugis kapag tinitingnan mula sa Earth!

A contact lens is a thin lens placed right on the front of the eye to fix blurry vision.

copy.bis:
Unsa ang contact lens?

Ang contact lens usa ka nipis nga lente nga gibutang direkta sa atubangan sa mata aron tul-iron ang hanap nga panan-aw.

Why do fisherfolk love the continental shelf?

The continental shelf is the shallow ocean floor around islands! Sunlight and nutrients reach everywhere here, making it the best fishing zone. The Philippines has a wide one!
copy.tl:
Bakit gusto ng mga mangingisda ang continental shelf?

Ang continental shelf ay ang mababaw na ocean floor sa paligid ng mga pulo! Ang araw at sustansya ay nakakarating dito, kaya ito ang pinakamagandang pangingisdang lugar. Malawak ang continental shelf ng Pilipinas!
copy.bis:
Nganong ganahan sa mga mangingisda ang continental shelf?

Ang continental shelf mao ang mabaw nga ocean floor sa palibot sa mga pulo! Ang adlaw ug sustansya makaabot dinhi, mao kini ang pinakamaayong lugar sa pangisda. Halapad ang continental shelf sa Pilipinas!

copy.en:
How is continental crust different from oceanic crust?

Continental crust, which forms the land, is thicker and lighter (made of granite). Oceanic crust beneath the seas is thinner and denser (made of basalt)!
copy.tl:
Paano naiiba ang continental crust sa oceanic crust?

Ang continental crust na pinagtatayuan ng lupa ay mas makapal at mas magaan (gawa sa granite). Ang oceanic crust sa ilalim ng karagatan ay mas manipis at mas mabigat (gawa sa basalt)!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa continental crust ug oceanic crust?

Ang continental crust nga gibarogan sa yuta mas baga ug mas gaan (hinimo sa granite). Ang oceanic crust sa ilawom sa kadagatan mas nipis ug mas bug-at (hinimo sa basalt)!

What happens inside a pot of boiling water?

Hot water near the flame rises, while cooler water on top sinks. This circular motion is convection — and it heats all the water!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa loob ng kumukulong tubig?

Umaakyat ang mainit na tubig malapit sa apoy, at bumababa ang mas malamig na tubig sa itaas. Ang paikot na galaw na ito ay convection — nagpapainit sa buong tubig!
copy.bis:
Unsay nahitabo sa nagbubukal nga tubig sa kaldero?

Mosaka ang init nga tubig duol sa kalayo, samtang mokunsad ang mas bugnaw nga tubig sa ibabaw. Kini nga paliyok nga paglihok mao ang convection — nag-init sa tibuok tubig!

copy.en: Air near the floor is cooler because cold air sinks to the bottom! That is why your feet feel cold even when the top of the room is warm.
copy.tl: Mas malamig ang hangin malapit sa sahig dahil bumababa ang malamig na hangin! Kaya malamig ang paa mo kahit init sa taas ng kwarto.
copy.bis: Mas bugnaw ang hangin duol sa salog tungod kay mokunsad ang bugnaw nga hangin! Mao nga bugnaw ang imong tiil bisan init sa taas sa kwarto.

Hot water at the bottom rises while cool water sinks! This creates convection currents that spread heat through the water.

Ang mainit na tubig sa ibaba ay umaangat habang ang malamig ay bumababa! Gumagawa ito ng convection currents na nagpapakalat ng init.
copy.bis:

Ang mainit nga tubig sa ubos misaka samtang ang malamig milugsong! Naghimo kini og convection currents nga nagpakaylap sa init sa tubig.

What forms when hot air keeps rising and cold air keeps sinking?

It forms a circular flow called a convection current! It carries heat from the warm part to the cold part.
copy.tl:

How does a coral reef get built?

A coral polyp builds a hard limestone skeleton around itself. When it dies, its skeleton stays, and new polyps grow on top — layer by layer, this builds the whole reef over thousands of years!
copy.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang coral reef?

Gumagawa ang coral polyp ng matigas na balangkas na limestone. Kapag namatay ito, naiiwan ang balangkas, at tumutubo ang bagong polyp sa ibabaw — patong-patong sa loob ng libong taon, ito ang bumubuo ng buong reef!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nga natukod ang coral reef?

Ang coral polyp mohimo og gahi nga balangkas nga limestone. Kon mamatay kini, magpabilin ang balangkas, ug motubo ang bag-ong polyp sa ibabaw — sapaw-sapaw sulod sa liboan ka tuig, mao kini ang nagtukod sa tibuok reef!

The Coral Triangle around the Philippines, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea holds over 2,000 kinds of reef fish — the richest ocean fish diversity on Earth.
copy.tl:
Saan matatagpuan ang pinakamaraming klase ng isda?

Ang Coral Triangle sa paligid ng Pilipinas, Indonesia, at Papua New Guinea ay may mahigit 2,000 uri ng isda sa dagat — ang pinakamaraming klase ng isda sa buong mundo.
copy.bis:
Asa makit-an ang pinakadaghang klase sa isda?

Ang Coral Triangle libot sa Pilipinas, Indonesia, ug Papua New Guinea adunay kapin sa 2,000 klase sa isda sa reef — ang pinakadaghang klase sa isda sa tibuok kalibutan.

It only explains a single phenomenon (bleaching) and does not support the competency's requirement to describe ecosystem features.

copy.en:
Why does bleached coral look white?

Once the colorful algae living inside are gone, only the coral's white skeleton shows through its clear tissue.
copy.tl:
Bakit puti ang bleached coral?

Namumuti ang coral dahil kapag wala na ang makukulay na algae, ang nakikita na lang ay ang puting kalansay nito sa ilalim ng malinaw na tisyu.
copy.bis:
Nganong puti ang bleached coral?

Moputi ang coral kay kon wala na ang mabulukon nga algae, ang puti nga kalansay na lang niini ang makita pinaagi sa tin-aw nga unod.

copy.en: Tiny algae live inside the coral, making food from sunlight and giving the coral its beautiful color!
copy.tl: May maliliit na algae na naninirahan sa loob ng coral, gumagawa ng pagkain mula sa sikat ng araw at nagbibigay ng kulay!
copy.bis: Adunay gagmay nga algae nga nagpuyo sulod sa coral, naghimo og pagkaon gikan sa kahayag sa adlaw ug naghatag og kolor!

copy.en: The Cordillera region is super rich in gold! It comes from hydrothermal ore deposits, where hot fluid from cooling magma flows through rock cracks and leaves gold behind.
copy.tl: Ang rehiyon ng Cordillera ay super mayaman sa ginto! Nanggagaling ito sa hydrothermal ore deposits, kung saan ang mainit na fluid mula sa cooling magma ay dumaan sa mga bitak ng bato at nag-iiwan ng ginto.
copy.bis: Ang rehiyon sa Cordillera super dato sa bulawan! Naggikan kini sa mga hydrothermal ore deposits, diin ang mainit nga fluid gikan sa nagbugnaw nga magma moagos sa mga bitak sa bato ug nagbilin sa bulawan.

copy.en: In places like China, fishermen train birds called cormorants to dive underwater and bring fish back to them.
copy.tl: Sa ilang lugar tulad ng China, sinasanay ng mga mangingisda ang cormorant para sumisid at magdala ng isda pabalik sa kanila.
copy.bis: Sa pipila ka lugar sama sa China, gibansay sa mga mananagat ang cormorant aron mosalom ug modala og isda balik kanila.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single classification fact (corn is a grass) but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups, nor does it support the skill of grouping based on similar characteristics. copy.en:
What plant family does corn belong to?

Corn is actually a kind of grass, just like rice and wheat — grown for its grain, which we turn into food.
copy.tl:
Anong pamilya ng halaman ang kinabibilangan ng mais?

Ang mais pala ay isang uri ng damo, tulad ng palay at trigo — itinatanim para sa butil nitong ginagawang pagkain.
copy.bis:
Unsang pamilya sa tanom nahisakop ang mais?

Ang mais diay usa ka matang sa sagbot, sama sa humay ug trigo — gipatubo alang sa lugas nga ginahimong pagkaon.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions atoms and elements (carbon, iron) but does not describe properties of pure substances, fixed chemical composition, or the unique number of protons per element. It is about the origin of atoms, not their properties.

assignedReviews.reason: The card names carbon and iron as examples but does not identify their symbols or teach element names/symbols from the periodic table. It does not directly support identifying the first 20 or common elements.

copy.en:
Are we really made of star stuff?

Yes! The atoms in our bodies like carbon and iron were forged inside stars by nuclear fusion and scattered by supernova explosions. We are literally made of star stuff!
copy.tl:
Gawa ba talaga tayo sa star stuff?

Oo! Ang mga atom sa ating katawan tulad ng carbon at iron ay ginawa sa loob ng mga bituin sa pamamagitan ng nuclear fusion at ibinulalas ng supernova explosions. Literal na gawa tayo sa star stuff!
copy.bis:
Gihimo ba gyud kita sa star stuff?

Oo! Ang mga atom sa atong lawas sama sa carbon ug iron gihimo sulod sa mga bituin pinaagi sa nuclear fusion ug gibulagak sa supernova explosions. Literal nga gihimo kita sa star stuff!

assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that covalent bonds form between nonmetals and gives water and carbon dioxide as examples. It does not explain the formation of the bond (e.g., sharing of electrons) as required by the competency.

copy.en:
What kind of atoms form covalent bonds?

They usually form between two nonmetals! Like hydrogen and oxygen in water, or carbon and oxygen in carbon dioxide.
copy.tl:
Anong uri ng mga atomo ang bumubuo ng covalent bonds?

Karaniwan silang nabubuo sa pagitan ng dalawang di-metal! Gaya ng hydrogen at oxygen sa tubig, o carbon at oxygen sa carbon dioxide.
copy.bis:
Unang klase sa mga atomo ang moporma og covalent bonds?

Kasagaran kini maporma tali sa duha ka dili-metal! Sama sa hydrogen ug oxygen sa tubig, o carbon ug oxygen sa carbon dioxide.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Covalent bonding creates small, separate molecules, but ionic bonding builds a huge repeating pattern of ions called a crystal lattice!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: show by using models that ionic compounds form crystalline structures whereas covalent compounds form individual molecules
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the conceptual difference between covalent molecules and ionic lattices, but the competency requires students to 'show by using models' that ionic compounds form crystalline structures whereas covalent compounds form individual molecules. The card does not involve or reference any model, so it does not directly support the model-based demonstration skill.

copy.en: Covalent bonding creates small, separate molecules, but ionic bonding builds a huge repeating pattern of ions called a crystal lattice!
copy.tl: Ang covalent bonding ay gumagawa ng maliliit na hiwalay na molekula, pero ang ionic bonding ay bumubuo ng malaking paulit-ulit na balangkas ng mga ion na tinatawag na crystal lattice!
copy.bis: Ang covalent bonding naghimo og gagmay nga mag-inusang molekula, apan ang ionic bonding nagtukod og dako nga balikbalik nga han-ay sa mga ion nga gitawag og crystal lattice!
